metadata.fee_info_2026: Standard fee €4.50/person/trail (general public). €3 with IFCN-protocol operators. PR1 (Vereda do Areeiro) is €10.50 (€7 with protocol operator) and excluded from multi-day passes. Madeira residents and children under 12 are exempt but must reserve via SIMplifica (simplifica.madeira.gov.pt). Some PR trails remain free (PR11 Vereda dos Balcões, PR13 Vereda do Fanal). Fees apply from 1 January 2026.
metadata.notes_on_links: AllTrails and Komoot URLs are deep links to the specific trail page where available. Where multiple AllTrails entries exist for the same PR code, the most-reviewed canonical page is preferred. Some lesser-known sub-routes do not have a dedicated AllTrails page; in those cases an AllTrails entry that covers the same physical route (e.g. an adjacent PR or combined route) is linked, or the field is set to null.
notes: v2 (2026-05-14): Added 3 non-PR / combined-PR trails (Levada Nova - Levada do Moinho; Rabaçal Lagoa do Vento combined PR 6.2/6.3/6.4 loop; Porto da Cruz → Caniçal via Vereda do Larano & Boca do Risco). Added `popularity`, `popularity_notes` and where available `alltrails_review_count` to every trail.

popularity_scale.Very High: Iconic must-do hikes; thousands of online reviews; on every 'best of Madeira' list; consistently very crowded.
popularity_scale.High: Well-known and frequently listed; often crowded in season.
popularity_scale.Medium: Appears in most guidebooks/blogs; moderate traffic.
popularity_scale.Low: Lesser-known; mostly seasoned hikers or locals; rarely crowded.
popularity_scale.Very Low: Hidden / obscure; very low traffic and minimal online coverage.
popularity_scale._methodology: Ratings combine: (a) AllTrails review counts where available, (b) frequency of appearance in top-N 'best Madeira hikes' lists from established travel blogs, (c) crowding/parking signals from recent reviews, and (d) general guidebook coverage. Within the PS PR (Porto Santo) set, ratings are relative to Porto Santo's overall smaller visitor base.

trails.name: Vereda do Areeiro
trails.alternative_names: Pico do Areeiro to Pico Ruivo
trails.highlights: Madeira's most iconic ridge walk across the island's highest peaks; crosses Pico das Torres (1,851m); tunnels carved through volcanic tuff; views of the central mountain massif from 1,800m+ above sea level
trails.equipment_needed: Proper hiking boots, layered clothing, headlamp (for tunnels), windproof and waterproof jacket, plenty of water (no sources on route), sun protection
trails.safety_notes: Exposed ridge sections with major drops on both sides; serious vertigo triggers; extremely weather-dependent; capacity limits via SIMplifica time slots after the April 2026 reopening; tickets are checked at the trailhead
trails.best_season: Year-round when open (reopened 27 April 2026 after wildfire reconstruction). Book early — slots sell out fast, especially 7:00–8:30 morning ones.
trails.parking_location: Pico do Areeiro car park
trails.exposure_notes: Very exposed ridge with major vertigo triggers; not suitable for those with fear of heights.
trails.popularity_notes: The iconic Areeiro-to-Ruivo ridge crossing; Madeira's signature hike. Featured on virtually every 'best of Madeira' list and consistently very crowded; requires fee + often advance reservation.

trails.name: Vereda da Ilha
trails.alternative_names: Ilha to Pico Ruivo
trails.highlights: Crosses two Natura 2000 ecosystems: the Central Mountain Massif (above 1,200m) and the UNESCO Laurisilva forest (400–1,200m); endemic birds (Madeira firecrest, chaffinch); panoramic views of the north coast and Ilha village
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots with grip, waterproof jacket, layered clothing for big altitude change, water (2L+), sun protection, walking poles helpful
trails.safety_notes: Steep climb of 1,376m elevation; sections can be very slippery and mossy after rain; long ascent demands good fitness; weather changes fast at altitude
trails.best_season: Spring and autumn for stable weather; year-round when conditions are dry
trails.parking_location: Ilha village (limited roadside parking)
trails.exposure_notes: Mostly sheltered laurel forest at lower altitudes; exposed slopes higher up; few cliff-edge sections
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda da Ilha (Ilha to Pico Ruivo) — popular alternative approach to Pico Ruivo; appears in most multi-day guides.

trails.name: Vereda do Pico Ruivo
trails.alternative_names: Achada do Teixeira to Pico Ruivo
trails.highlights: Shortest route to Madeira's highest peak; Homem em Pé basalt rock formation; connects to PR1, PR1.1 and PR1.3 at Casa de Abrigo do Pico Ruivo; sea-of-clouds views
trails.equipment_needed: Layers (cold/wind), water, sturdy shoes, windproof jacket
trails.safety_notes: Weather changes fast at altitude; start early; can be dangerous in strong winds; ground is slippery when wet
trails.parking_location: Achada do Teixeira
trails.exposure_notes: Mountain route with steep sections; exposure varies with weather and visibility
trails.popularity_notes: Direct access to Madeira's highest peak (1,862 m). Among the most-hiked routes on the island, listed in nearly every top-10 guide.

trails.name: Vereda da Encumeada
trails.alternative_names: Pico Ruivo to Encumeada ridge traverse
trails.start_point: Casa de Abrigo do Pico Ruivo (1,764m)
trails.highlights: Follows the central mountain range westward from the highest peak; Furna da Lapa da Cadela cave; transition between high-altitude heath and Laurisilva forest; panoramic central-island views
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots, hard-shell windproof jacket (exposed to north and south winds), 2L+ water (no water source on the ridge), warm layers, sun hat, hiking poles
trails.safety_notes: Closed since August 2024 due to wildfire damage and subsequent landslides; multiple ascents and descents at 1,000–1,800m altitude; ridge fully exposed to weather
trails.best_season: Spring to early autumn (when reopened); avoid winter fog and high wind
trails.parking_location: Achada do Teixeira (start) / Encumeada Snack Bar (end) — recommend pre-arranged taxi as start and end are 1.5h drive apart
trails.exposure_notes: Very exposed ridge crossing the central mountain massif; landslide-damaged railings; not suitable for vertigo sufferers
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda da Encumeada — frequently chained with PR1 by ambitious hikers; well known among the trail-runner community.

trails.name: Vereda do Urzal
trails.alternative_names: Urzal Trail, Curral das Freiras to Boaventura
trails.start_point: Fajã dos Cardos, Curral das Freiras (519m)
trails.end_point: Lombo do Urzal, Boaventura (1,450m peak at Boca das Torrinhas)
trails.highlights: South-to-north coast crossing; Boca das Torrinhas viewpoint at 1,450m with views of Pico Ruivo and Curral das Freiras valley; connects to PR1.3; ancient Royal Path of carriers; Laurisilva forest descent
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots, layers (altitude up to 1,450m), 2L+ water, sun protection, rain jacket, hiking poles for steep descent
trails.safety_notes: Steep climbs and descents; northern (Boaventura) side often muddy and slippery; southern (Curral) ascent sometimes affected by falling rocks; check current status before going
trails.best_season: Spring and autumn (avoid winter fog at altitude)
trails.parking_location: Fajã dos Cardos (Curral das Freiras) or Lombo do Urzal (Boaventura)
trails.exposure_notes: Mountain ridge crossing with exposed sections near Boca das Torrinhas; take care in wind and fog
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda do Urzal — a known northern levada hike but less Instagram-famous; appears in serious hiking guides rather than mainstream lists.

trails.name: Vereda do Burro
trails.alternative_names: Donkey Trail, Pico do Areeiro to Ribeira das Cales
trails.end_point: Ribeira das Cales — Funchal Ecological Park Welcome Centre (1,130m)
trails.highlights: Poço da Neve igloo-shaped ice house (1813); high-altitude flora; views of Ribeira do Cidrão valley flowing into Curral das Freiras; Paul da Serra plateau visible on clear days
trails.equipment_needed: Warm layers, windproof jacket, sturdy shoes, water
trails.safety_notes: High altitude start (1,805m) means cold and windy conditions common; mostly downhill so easier on the knees than uphill
trails.parking_location: Pico do Areeiro car park (with shuttle/taxi from Ribeira das Cales if doing one-way)
trails.exposure_notes: Mostly downhill with moderate exposure; the start near Pico do Areeiro is exposed to wind
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda do Burro — moderate traffic; on dedicated Madeira hiking sites but not in most top-10 lists.

trails.name: Caminho Real do Monte
trails.alternative_names: Royal Path of Monte, Ribeira das Cales to Monte
trails.highlights: Crosses Levada das Cales (1784); Pico Alto viewpoint at 1,129m with panoramic Funchal views; ancient cobblestone Royal Path; Monte Palace gardens and Mother Church at the finish; the Wicker Toboggans of Monte nearby
trails.equipment_needed: Shoes with strong grip (basalt cobblestones are notoriously slippery, even dry), walking sticks, water, camera
trails.safety_notes: Ancient basalt cobblestones are slippery dry, treacherous when wet; uneven steps; very steep — knee-stressing on descent
trails.parking_location: Ribeira das Cales (start) or use Monte cable car / bus 22 from Funchal
trails.exposure_notes: Forest path with photogenic city views; low exposure overall
trails.popularity_notes: Caminho Real do Monte — short historic cobbled trail from Monte; not in most lists, mostly done as a side excursion.

trails.name: Levada do Barreiro
trails.alternative_names: Barreiro Levada, Poço da Neve Trail
trails.highlights: Poço da Neve ice house (1813); panoramic Funchal views; high-altitude flora; Ribeira de Santa Luzia valley; signed connection to Ribeira das Cales
trails.equipment_needed: Comfortable walking shoes, water, warm layer
trails.safety_notes: Mostly downhill, easy path. Currently partial opening only — check trail status before hiking.
trails.parking_location: Poço da Neve area
trails.exposure_notes: Low exposure; gentle levada path suitable for most fitness levels
trails.popularity_notes: Levada do Barreiro — Paúl da Serra plateau levada; remote, lesser known.

trails.name: Vereda das Funduras
trails.alternative_names: Funduras Trail, Portela to Maroços
trails.highlights: Penha d'Águia (Eagle Rock) views, Laurisilva forest, green hills of Machico, much less crowded alternative to flagship trails
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots, water, sun protection, light rain layer
trails.safety_notes: Steep descent sections; can be slippery when wet; some narrow trail sections; less maintained than flagship trails
trails.parking_location: Portela Viewpoint
trails.exposure_notes: Moderate exposure at viewpoints; mostly forest paths with some open hillside sections
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda das Funduras — eastern Madeira laurel-forest loop; covered by hiking blogs, low-to-medium traffic.

trails.name: Levada das 25 Fontes
trails.alternative_names: 25 Springs, Rabaçal Levada Walk
trails.highlights: 25 natural springs feeding a lagoon, waterfalls, UNESCO Laurisilva forest, geosite C01; one-way circulation on the return via Bypass route
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots, headlamp (for the bypass tunnel), rain jacket, water
trails.safety_notes: Bypass tunnel (~800m, headlamp required); narrow sections with drops on one side; one of the most crowded trails — arrive early; partially one-way controlled
trails.best_season: Year-round (best waterflow in spring and after rain)
trails.parking_location: Rabaçal car park (shuttle available down the access road)
trails.exposure_notes: Mostly forest paths, but includes narrow sections and unprotected drops in places
trails.popularity_notes: Levada das 25 Fontes — the island's most famous levada walk. Always near the top of 'must-do Madeira hikes' lists; busy year-round (shuttle now required from Rabaçal car park).

trails.name: Levada do Risco
trails.alternative_names: Risco Waterfall
trails.highlights: Two-tier 100m waterfall; popular easy add-on to PR6; same starting point as 25 Fontes
trails.equipment_needed: Comfortable shoes, light rain layer, water
trails.safety_notes: Slippery after rain; watch footing near viewpoints; very busy in summer
trails.parking_location: Rabaçal car park
trails.exposure_notes: Short, popular walk; take care at viewpoints and on slippery sections
trails.popularity_notes: Levada do Risco — short walk to a 100 m waterfall, almost always done alongside PR6; high foot traffic.

trails.name: Levada do Alecrim
trails.alternative_names: Rosemary Levada, Lagoa Dona Beja Trail
trails.highlights: Flat, less-crowded alternative to PR6; heather tunnels; sweeping views over Rabaçal valley and Ribeira da Janela; Dona Beja lagoon at the source (feeds Lagoa do Vento waterfall); can be combined with PR6.3 as a loop
trails.equipment_needed: Comfortable hiking shoes, water, light rain layer; no headlamp needed
trails.safety_notes: Flat with very little elevation change; can be muddy in places after rain
trails.parking_location: Rabaçal car park
trails.exposure_notes: Sheltered forest levada with very low exposure
trails.popularity_notes: Levada do Alecrim — quiet Rabaçal-area levada; often combined with PR6.3 (Lagoa do Vento) or PR6.4.

trails.name: Vereda da Lagoa do Vento
trails.alternative_names: Wind Lagoon Path
trails.highlights: Tranquil rain-basin lagoon at the top of Risco waterfall; transition zone between high-altitude heath and Laurisilva forest; can loop with PR6.2 Levada do Alecrim
trails.equipment_needed: Sturdy shoes (rough dirt and roots), water, windbreaker (it's literally called the Wind Lagoon)
trails.safety_notes: Steep descent on rugged dirt path; very slippery when wet; not as developed as flagship trails
trails.parking_location: Rabaçal car park
trails.exposure_notes: Mostly sheltered; care needed at the lagoon edge above Risco fall
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda da Lagoa do Vento — descent to a hidden waterfall lake; small but growing online following.

trails.name: Levada Velha do Rabaçal
trails.alternative_names: Old Rabaçal Levada, The Forgotten Route
trails.highlights: Quieter alternative route sitting above the main Risco levada; Túnel das Estrebarias (Furado Velho, built 1855 — first water tunnel crossing from north to south coast); great unobstructed views of Rabaçal basin and the Risco waterfall from above; UNESCO Laurisilva forest
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots, long pants (some bushes), water, windbreaker, GPS/offline map (entrance is not well-marked)
trails.safety_notes: Less maintained than flagship trails; can be muddy; access path involves an 800m walk from ER 105
trails.parking_location: Pico Gordo / Pico da Urze area (ER 105)
trails.exposure_notes: Mostly forest, with some exposed contour sections above the Rabaçal valley
trails.popularity_notes: Levada Velha do Rabaçal — old levada section; specialist hike, very limited online coverage.

trails.name: Vereda do Pico Fernandes
trails.alternative_names: Pico Fernandes Path, Paul da Serra to 25 Fontes
trails.highlights: Old footpath descending from the Paul da Serra plateau to 25 Fontes; 360° views from Pico Fernandes at 1,400m on clear days, including Pico da Urze dam; high-altitude heath transitioning to laurel forest; very quiet alternative access to 25 Fontes
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots, water, sun protection, layers (high-altitude weather changes fast)
trails.safety_notes: Steep descent in places; less maintained than the main Rabaçal trails; weather highly variable at altitude
trails.best_season: Spring to autumn (clear-weather days for the panoramic views)
trails.parking_location: Roadside on ER 209 at Paul da Serra
trails.exposure_notes: Exposed plateau with no shade at the top; descent partially sheltered
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda do Pico Fernandes — minor Rabaçal-area path; almost no online write-ups.

trails.name: Vereda do Túnel do Cavalo
trails.alternative_names: Horse Tunnel Path, Furado Novo, Furado das 25 Fontes
trails.start_point: Caldeira leisure area (Garagem), Estrada Dr. Roberto Monteiro (1,055m)
trails.highlights: 800m-long Túnel do Cavalo (built 1863–1877); historic Calheta-power-station water tunnel; bypasses the busy Rabaçal road and shuttle; emerges into dense Laurisilva on the north side — a 'Jurassic Park' moment
trails.equipment_needed: Headlamp/flashlight essential (the tunnel is dark, humid, and uneven), waterproof shoes (tunnel floor often has puddles), light jacket (tunnel is drafty and cold)
trails.safety_notes: Tunnel floor is wet, slippery, and uneven; no lighting; not suitable for those with claustrophobia; phone torches work but a real headlamp is far better
trails.parking_location: Small roadside parking at Caldeira on Estrada Dr. Roberto Monteiro
trails.exposure_notes: Forest path with low exposure; the long tunnel can feel intense for first-time tunnel hikers
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda do Túnel do Cavalo — obscure short route; minimal online presence.

trails.name: Levada do Paul II - Um caminho para todos
trails.alternative_names: A Path for Everyone, Paul II Accessible Levada
trails.highlights: Flat, wide, smooth-surface trail designed for wheelchairs, strollers, and walkers; views south over the Calheta lombos and the Paul da Serra plateau; often above the clouds at 1,400m; gorse-bloom landscape
trails.equipment_needed: Comfortable walking shoes/wheelchair, warm layer (high altitude), light rain layer
trails.safety_notes: No steps; almost entirely flat; suitable for people with motor disabilities and families with young children
trails.best_season: Year-round (gorse bloom adds yellow contrast in spring)
trails.parking_location: Layby on ER 110 at Paul da Serra; signed PR 6.8
trails.exposure_notes: Exposed plateau but flat and protected on the accessible-path side; high-altitude weather can change fast
trails.popularity_notes: Levada do Paul II (accessibility-focused 'um caminho para todos') — recent, very low traffic.

trails.name: Levada do Moinho
trails.alternative_names: Mill Levada, Ribeira da Cruz to Lamaceiros
trails.highlights: Historic water mills, Laurisilva forest, Achadas mill ruins, agricultural landscape transition
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots, rain jacket, water
trails.safety_notes: Closed since June 2024 due to landslide damage. When open: can be muddy and overgrown in sections.
trails.parking_location: Ribeira da Cruz
trails.exposure_notes: Low to moderate exposure; mainly forest and levada path. Some narrow sections near drops.
trails.popularity_notes: Levada do Moinho (the official PR7, Ribeira da Cruz – Lamaceiros) — distinct from the popular AllTrails Levada Nova/Moinho loop; moderate traffic.

trails.name: Vereda da Ponta de São Lourenço
trails.alternative_names: São Lourenço Peninsula, Dragon's Tail, Eastern Peninsula
trails.end_point: Casa do Sardinha / Ponta do Furado (23m)
trails.highlights: Volcanic coastal peninsula with red basalt cliffs; views of Desembarcadouro and Farol islets; possible monk seal sightings; partial Nature Reserve; Cais do Sardinha cafe and beach near the end
trails.equipment_needed: Sun protection (no shade), windproof layer, plenty of water (2L+), sturdy shoes for loose gravel
trails.safety_notes: No shade, strong winds, exposed drops; final steep climb to Miradouro do Ponta do Furado; no swimming after rough seas
trails.best_season: October to May for cooler temps; avoid windy days; start very early in summer
trails.parking_location: Baía d'Abra car park (free, fills quickly)
trails.exposure_notes: Exposed coastal sections with unprotected edges; avoid in strong wind; no shade anywhere
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda da Ponta de São Lourenço — the only volcanic peninsula hike, fully exposed. Iconic, heavily featured in guides; very crowded from late morning onward.

trails.name: Levada do Caldeirão Verde
trails.alternative_names: Green Cauldron, Queimadas Levada
trails.highlights: 100m waterfall into an emerald pool; thatched-roof Santana houses at Queimadas; 18th-century historic levada; jungle immersion through Laurisilva forest; optional extension to Caldeirão do Inferno (currently closed beyond Caldeirão Verde)
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots, headlamp (4 tunnels), rain gear, water, snacks
trails.safety_notes: Four dark tunnels; headlamp essential; narrow ledges with drops on one side; current closure of section between Caldeirão Verde and Caldeirão do Inferno
trails.best_season: Year-round (waterfalls best in winter and spring)
trails.parking_location: Queimadas Forest Park
trails.exposure_notes: Includes narrow ledges and multiple dark tunnels; take extra care in wet weather
trails.popularity_notes: Levada do Caldeirão Verde — flagship 'green cauldron' levada with tunnels and waterfall. Consistently in top-5 Madeira lists.

trails.name: Levada do Caldeirão Verde - um caminho para todos
trails.alternative_names: A Path for Everyone (Queimadas to Pico das Pedras)
trails.highlights: Wide, flat trail through transition zone between Madeira's UNESCO Laurisilva and exotic forest; accessible to wheelchairs, strollers, and walkers; visit to the Casa das Tradições Madeirenses (Santana thatched house traditions)
trails.equipment_needed: Comfortable shoes (sneakers fine), warm layer (damp/cool in forest), camera
trails.safety_notes: Wide, safe, completely flat; perfect for families with young children, elderly visitors, and anyone wanting a relaxing forest bathe
trails.parking_location: Queimadas Park (busy) or Pico das Pedras (quieter, better for wheelchair access)
trails.exposure_notes: Sheltered forest path with no exposure; mystical when fog rolls through trees
trails.popularity_notes: Caldeirão Verde accessibility-focused 'um caminho para todos' — a short ADA-style section of PR9, very low review count.

trails.name: Levada do Furado
trails.alternative_names: Ribeiro Frio to Portela, Furado Levada Walk
trails.highlights: One of Madeira's oldest levadas, deep Laurisilva forest immersion, Ribeiro Frio trout farm at the start, panoramic finish at Portela viewpoint
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots, rain jacket, water, warm layer
trails.safety_notes: Section between Ribeiro Frio and Lamaceiros has been periodically closed due to landslides; check current status; narrow sections, can be muddy
trails.parking_location: Ribeiro Frio
trails.exposure_notes: Mostly low-exposure forest path; some narrow levada sections with drops on one side
trails.popularity_notes: Levada do Furado (Ribeiro Frio – Portela) — classic long levada through laurissilva, in most island guides.

trails.name: Vereda dos Balcões
trails.alternative_names: Balcões Viewpoint, Ribeiro Frio Balcony
trails.highlights: Panoramic central-peaks viewpoint (Pico do Areeiro, Pico das Torres, Pico Ruivo on clear days); endemic Madeira chaffinches at the viewpoint; Fajã da Nogueira hydroelectric plant visible; Ribeiro Frio trout farm nearby
trails.equipment_needed: Comfortable shoes, camera, optionally bird seed (note feeding wildlife is discouraged)
trails.safety_notes: Easy, well-maintained path (watch for wet spots); parking very limited and chaotic in peak season — come early
trails.parking_location: Ribeiro Frio (very limited; roadside parking common)
trails.exposure_notes: Easy forest path; the viewpoint itself can feel high even though it is fenced
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda dos Balcões — short, easy, family-friendly viewpoint walk near Ribeiro Frio; one of the most-visited short walks on Madeira.

trails.name: Caminho Real da Encumeada
trails.alternative_names: Royal Path of Encumeada, Boca da Corrida to Encumeada
trails.highlights: Historic cobbled royal path crossing the central mountain massif; views of Pico Grande, Pico Ruivo, and the Nuns Valley; spectacular ridge walk
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots, warm layers, 2L+ water, rain jacket
trails.safety_notes: Partially open from January 2026 — passable only from Boca da Corrida to km 3.5 (Relvinhas); beyond Relvinhas closed due to landslides; mountain weather changes rapidly
trails.best_season: Spring to autumn (clear days for peak views)
trails.parking_location: Boca da Corrida Viewpoint
trails.exposure_notes: Mountain traverse with exposed ridge sections; significant weather exposure at altitude
trails.popularity_notes: Caminho Real da Encumeada — long traverse, rarely done in full; quiet.

trails.name: Vereda do Fanal
trails.alternative_names: Fanal Forest Trail, Assobiadores to Fanal
trails.highlights: UNESCO Laurisilva forest, the iconic misty Fanal Forest with ancient twisted Ocotea Foetens (Til) trees; viewpoints over Rabaçal valley and Chão da Ribeira; Sítio do Fio old cable installation; small volcanic caldera (Reserve of Rest and Silence)
trails.equipment_needed: Waterproof shoes, warm layer (often foggy), water; visibility can drop suddenly so an offline map helps
trails.safety_notes: Can be muddy and slippery; visibility can drop in fog; some steep stair sections; signage less frequent than flagship trails
trails.best_season: Year-round (especially atmospheric in winter when foggy)
trails.parking_location: Fanal parking area or Assobiadores roadside
trails.exposure_notes: Low exposure; main challenge is mud and poor visibility in fog
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda do Fanal — famous misty laurel forest, heavily Instagrammed; very crowded on foggy days.

trails.name: Vereda da Palha Carga
trails.alternative_names: Palha Carga Path, Louro da Gota to 25 Fontes
trails.highlights: Less-known shortcut to 25 Fontes via high-altitude heath; named after the endemic Palha-carga grass (Festuca donax); impressive views over Rabaçal valley and Ribeira da Janela; crosses Ribeira dos Cedros to join Levada das 25 Fontes
trails.equipment_needed: Waterproof boots (often muddy), GPS/offline map (signage less frequent), water, layers
trails.safety_notes: Steep descent into 25 Fontes; less maintained than main PR13 route; signage limited
trails.parking_location: Roadside on ER 209 near Louro da Gota
trails.exposure_notes: Open plateau at the top, then sheltered descent through forest
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda da Palha Carga — obscure spur near Fanal.

trails.name: Levada dos Cedros
trails.alternative_names: Cedar Levada, Fanal Forest Walk
trails.highlights: Levada built in the 17th century — one of the oldest on the island; deep UNESCO Laurisilva forest with ancient cedar and laurel; small waterfall pool at the source; views into the Ribeira da Janela valley
trails.equipment_needed: Waterproof shoes (often muddy), warm layer (often foggy), water, walking stick
trails.safety_notes: Can be muddy and slippery especially in the middle section; fog reduces visibility; staircase at one end can be steep
trails.parking_location: Fanal area or roadside on ER 209 at Curral Falso
trails.exposure_notes: Very low exposure; sheltered forest levada path
trails.popularity_notes: Levada dos Cedros — pretty forest levada in the northwest, in most thorough guides.

trails.name: Vereda da Ribeira da Janela
trails.alternative_names: Ribeira da Janela Valley Trail
trails.highlights: Historic footpath, valley descent with sea views, connection to PR14 Levada dos Cedros; perfect when combined with Fanal Forest and PR14 as a 19km loop
trails.equipment_needed: Sturdy shoes (steep descent), trekking poles helpful, water
trails.safety_notes: Steep descent (420m drop in 2.7km) — knee strain on descent; harder uphill; can be slippery when wet; long staircase section
trails.parking_location: Curral Falso (Fanal) or Ribeira da Janela village
trails.exposure_notes: Steep descent with some exposed hillside sections; moderate vertigo potential
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda da Ribeira da Janela — quiet northwestern valley walk.

trails.name: Levada Fajã do Rodrigues
trails.alternative_names: São Vicente Levada, Ginjas Levada Walk
trails.end_point: Ribeira do Inferno / Ribeira da Janela
trails.highlights: Three tunnels (longest ~20–25 min walk); dramatic Ribeira do Inferno valley; abundant water source for São Vicente; less crowded than flagship trails
trails.equipment_needed: Headlamp (essential for tunnels), hiking boots, rain jacket, warm layer, GPS/offline map
trails.safety_notes: Long dark tunnel (20–25 min), uneven footing, dripping water; narrow exposed sections on the valley side
trails.parking_location: Ginjas, São Vicente
trails.exposure_notes: Long tunnels require confidence; narrow levada path with drops in sections
trails.popularity_notes: Levada Fajã do Rodrigues — São Vicente valley levada with tunnels; appears in adventure-hike write-ups.

trails.name: Caminho do Pináculo e Folhadal
trails.alternative_names: Pináculo Trail, Encumeada Loop, Lombo do Mouro to Encumeada
trails.start_point: Boca da Encumeada / Lombo do Mouro
trails.end_point: Boca da Encumeada / Bica da Cana
trails.highlights: Jurassic Park-style scenery, jagged peaks, levada tunnels, cascading waterfalls, ridge walk; on clear days views of São Vicente valley, Pico do Areeiro and Pico Ruivo
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking boots, headlamp (tunnels), warm layers, rain jacket, 2L+ water and food
trails.safety_notes: Currently only the section between Encumeada and Bica da Cana is passable (between km 0 and km 4.3 closed); long and demanding even in full opening; exposed ridges and tunnels
trails.best_season: Spring to autumn (clear weather essential for ridge sections)
trails.parking_location: Boca da Encumeada or Bica da Cana
trails.exposure_notes: Exposed ridge walk sections; long tunnels; significant altitude changes; not for vertigo sufferers
trails.popularity_notes: Caminho do Pináculo e Folhadal — popular among locals and serious hikers; great viewpoints.

trails.name: Levada do Rei
trails.alternative_names: King's Levada, Quebradas to Ribeiro Bonito
trails.start_point: São Jorge Wastewater Treatment Plant, Quebradas (535m)
trails.highlights: Deep Laurisilva forest immersion, waterfalls, walk-through cascade, hidden gorge with main waterfall at end; centuries-old São Jorge water mill at the start (still in operation); much less crowded than PR6 or PR9
trails.equipment_needed: Comfortable hiking shoes, water, rain layer, optional flashlight (two very short tunnels)
trails.safety_notes: Some narrow sections; trail can be wet and muddy; one section passes under a small waterfall — light shower expected
trails.parking_location: Quinta Levada do Rei (small lot near trailhead in Quebradas)
trails.exposure_notes: Generally low exposure, but keep awareness near levada edges, especially when wet
trails.popularity_notes: Levada do Rei — laurel-forest end-to-source walk in São Jorge; classic but quieter than the headliners.

trails.name: Caminho Real do Paul do Mar
trails.alternative_names: Royal Path to Paúl do Mar
trails.highlights: Historic zigzag royal path with stone steps; sweeping sea views; Lombo da Rocha viewpoint over Jardim do Mar and Paúl do Mar; agricultural terraces; finishes in the small fishing village of Paúl do Mar
trails.equipment_needed: Sturdy shoes with grip, trekking poles helpful, water, sun protection
trails.safety_notes: Very steep descent (534m in 1.8km); hard on knees; cobbled stone steps can be slippery (worn smooth); return uphill is extremely demanding — many opt for taxi back
trails.best_season: Year-round (avoid in heavy rain — slippery stones)
trails.parking_location: Prazeres
trails.exposure_notes: Steep coastal descent with exposure on the hillside; vertigo-inducing in sections
trails.popularity_notes: Caminho Real do Paul do Mar — historic cobbled descent to the coast; in most thorough guides.

trails.name: Vereda do Jardim do Mar
trails.alternative_names: Garden of the Sea Trail, Prazeres to Jardim do Mar
trails.highlights: Jardim do Mar and Paúl do Mar views; agricultural terraces (poios) along stone walls; historic path; descent through dry Laurissilva with barbusano and Canary bay trees
trails.equipment_needed: Sturdy shoes, sun protection, water
trails.safety_notes: Closed since August 2024 due to landslide damage. When open: steep descent through terraces, narrow path sections.
trails.parking_location: Prazeres
trails.exposure_notes: Hillside descent with moderate exposure; some sections overlook steep drops
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda do Jardim do Mar — short coastal-cliff walk near Paul do Mar; locally well-known.

trails.name: Caminho do Norte
trails.alternative_names: North Path, Encumeada to Ribeira Grande
trails.highlights: Traditional stone path connecting north and south of the island, used historically by farmers; Madeira forest area
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking shoes, water, light rain layer
trails.safety_notes: Steep and slippery when wet; generally wide path
trails.parking_location: Encumeada
trails.exposure_notes: Some steep sections but generally wide path
trails.popularity_notes: Caminho do Norte — long historic route; very low traffic.

trails.name: Vereda do Chão dos Louros
trails.alternative_names: Laurel Floor Path (Circular)
trails.highlights: Circular laurel-forest walk with streamside paths, picnic and barbecue area, camping, and a viewpoint over the São Vicente valley — ideal for families
trails.equipment_needed: Comfortable shoes, rain jacket (light rain common), picnic supplies if grilling
trails.safety_notes: Stream crossing requires stepping across rocks; west section has fewer markers — follow standard hiking signs attentively
trails.best_season: Year-round (picnic area busiest in summer, especially 1 May)
trails.parking_location: Chão dos Louros Forest Park
trails.exposure_notes: No exposure; suitable for children and beginners
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda do Chão dos Louros — quiet Encumeada-area picnic-forest walk.

trails.name: Glaciar de Planalto
trails.alternative_names: Plateau Glacier Trail, Bica da Cana Geological Loop
trails.highlights: Geomorphological evidence of a Last Glacial Maximum ice field (~25,000 years ago); U-shaped glacial valley; basaltic cinder cone of Fonte do Juncal (Middle Pleistocene volcanic eruption); Miradouro das Rabaças viewpoint over the Ribeira da Ponta do Sol valley; ruins of corrals at Sítio das Pedras
trails.equipment_needed: Sturdy footwear, sun protection (no shade), water, layers, hiking poles
trails.safety_notes: Open plateau exposed to wind and sun; overgrown paths in places; little shade; weather changes fast at altitude
trails.best_season: Spring to autumn (when reopened) — clear days for the panoramic geological views
trails.parking_location: Bica da Cana parking area
trails.exposure_notes: Fully exposed high-altitude plateau with no shade or shelter
trails.popularity_notes: Glaciar de Planalto — niche geological-interest path on Paúl da Serra plateau.

trails.name: Levada da Rocha Vermelha
trails.alternative_names: Red Rock Levada, Água do Vimieiro
trails.highlights: One of the longest single tunnels on the island (~1.6–2 km); spectacular views down the Rabaçal valley; multiple waterfalls along the levada (some flow onto the path); much quieter than PR6 with views of the Rabaçal valley from below 25 Fontes
trails.equipment_needed: Headlamp essential (very long dark tunnel); waterproof jacket (you will get wet from waterfalls); hiking boots; water and snacks
trails.safety_notes: Closed since March 2026 due to landslides and terrain instability from erosion; long dark tunnel is wet underfoot and requires concentration; uneven surfaces beside levada with significant drop-offs
trails.parking_location: Fanal area on ER 209
trails.exposure_notes: Narrow levada path with deep drop-offs into Rabaçal valley; long dark tunnel; not for vertigo or claustrophobia sufferers
trails.popularity_notes: Levada da Rocha Vermelha — remote, rarely walked.

trails.name: Vereda do Pico Branco e Terra Chã
trails.alternative_names: PR1 Porto Santo, White Peak and Flat Land Trail
trails.highlights: Porto Santo's most-recommended hike; two iconic viewpoints — Pico Branco (the island's second-highest peak) and Terra Chã (over the dramatic green-and-blue northern coast); Natura 2000 Habitats Directive zone; endemic flora including dragon trees and laurel shrubs; Cory's Shearwater and Common Tern bird colonies; Furna dos Homiziados pirate-era hideout
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking shoes with grip, water, sun protection, jacket for wind
trails.safety_notes: Steep, steady ascent — moderately challenging but manageable; uneven rocky paths in places; little shade; can be windy at the peaks
trails.best_season: Year-round; spring brings wildflowers; avoid midday in summer
trails.parking_location: Gravel lot next to the trailhead on ER 111
trails.exposure_notes: Exposed ridge sections with strong winds; views over high cliffs
trails.popularity_notes: Vereda do Pico Branco e Terra Chã — Porto Santo's top PR hike; high relative popularity within Porto Santo but small absolute review counts due to the island's lower visitation.

trails.name: Vereda do Pico do Castelo
trails.alternative_names: Castle Peak Trail (PR2 Porto Santo)
trails.end_point: Miradouro do Pico do Castelo (437m) / circular back to Moledo
trails.highlights: Circular trail looping around Pico do Facho (517m — island's highest point) before climbing Pico do Castelo (437m); 360° panoramic views of Porto Santo and the Atlantic, with Madeira visible on clear days; bust of Schiappa de Azevedo (early-20th-century reforestation pioneer); volcanic crater with 16th-century fortress ruins
trails.equipment_needed: Hiking shoes with grip, water, sun protection (limited shade), windbreaker for the summit
trails.safety_notes: Uneven and sometimes loose terrain on the gravel and dirt track; can feel exposed near the summit
trails.best_season: Spring and autumn for cooler hiking weather; avoid summer midday heat
trails.parking_location: Moledo trailhead (ER 111)
trails.exposure_notes: Reforested slopes provide some shade; summit and ridges are wind-exposed
trails.popularity_notes: Porto Santo's Vereda do Pico do Castelo — overshadowed by PS PR1; low traffic.

trails.name: Levada do Pico do Castelo
trails.alternative_names: Castle Peak Levada (PR3 Porto Santo)
trails.end_point: Capela de Nossa Senhora da Graça (80m)
trails.highlights: 20th-century agricultural levada; views of Porto Santo's southern coast and Ilhéu de Baixo islet; endemic heather (Erica platycodon) and Aleppo poplars (Populus alba); 1530s Capela de Nossa Senhora da Graça (rebuilt 1951), one of the oldest religious buildings on Porto Santo; popular pilgrimage on August 15
trails.equipment_needed: Comfortable walking shoes, water, sun protection
trails.safety_notes: Currently the 530m tunnel section is closed; section between Camacha and Capela da Graça is open and walkable
trails.best_season: Year-round; mild and dry climate makes Porto Santo trails accessible most of the year
trails.parking_location: Camacha (start) — ER 120 roadside
trails.exposure_notes: Mostly open hillside; minimal shade; relatively low altitude so wind/weather is mild
trails.popularity_notes: Porto Santo's Levada do Pico do Castelo — easy walk along an old aqueduct; locally known, low traffic.

trails.name: Levada Nova - Levada do Moinho
alternative_names: Levada Nova / Levada do Moinho Loop
trails.start_point: Near the church in Ponta do Sol / Lombada da Ponta do Sol
highlights: Walk-behind double waterfall on Levada Nova
Old watermill ruins along Levada do Moinho
Panoramic upper levada with valley and ocean views
River crossings and traditional poios (terraced farmland)
equipment_needed: Trekking poles helpful for river crossings
Sturdy shoes with good grip (paths can be muddy)
trails.safety_notes: Upper Levada Nova has narrow, exposed sections with steep drops; some railings reported missing. Not recommended for people with severe vertigo. Avoid after heavy rain (flooding/slippery). Street parking only near the church and it fills fast — arrive early.
trails.best_season: Year-round; spring and autumn are quietest.
trails.parking_location: Street parking near the church in Lombada da Ponta do Sol; very limited.
trails.exposure_rating: High (on the upper Levada Nova section)
trails.exposure_notes: Lower Levada do Moinho is well-shaded and protected. The upper Levada Nova has long narrow stretches with vertical drops; some sections have damaged or missing railings.

tunnels.notes: One long rock-cut tunnel on Levada Nova with low ceilings in places; headlamp strongly recommended.

trails.popularity_notes: Among the most-reviewed non-PR Madeira trails on AllTrails (4.7/5, 5,478+ reviews) and almost universally listed in 'best Madeira levada walks' blog posts. AllTrails describes the area as 'very busy'; parking fills rapidly.

trails.name: Rabaçal Loop — Lagoa do Vento (PR 6.2 / 6.3 / 6.4)
trails.location: Rabaçal, Paúl da Serra plateau (central-west Madeira)
trails.status: Open (combined route over existing PR sections; depends on each component's status)
trails.start_point: Rabaçal car park (top, off ER110 / Paúl da Serra)
trails.fee_amount: PR 6.2, PR 6.3 and PR 6.4 each carry the standard €3 PR access fee (paid per trail per day). Check current status of each PR before going.
highlights: Levada do Alecrim — quiet, mossy laurissilva levada (PR 6.2)
Descent to Lagoa do Vento — hidden waterfall lake at the head of a steep valley (PR 6.3)
Wind Peak viewpoint with valley framing (komoot highlight)
Levada Velha do Rabaçal — historic upper levada section (PR 6.4)
Combines three official PRs into a single satisfying day
equipment_needed: Trekking poles useful on the Lagoa do Vento descent
Layers — Paúl da Serra weather is unpredictable
trails.safety_notes: Off-grid segment for ~161 m after 10.4 km — navigation care needed. The Lagoa do Vento descent is steep and can be slippery when wet. Check each component PR's status (open/closed) before setting out via the official Visit Madeira PR navigator.
trails.best_season: Late spring to early autumn (the Paúl da Serra plateau gets cold and foggy in winter).
trails.parking_location: Rabaçal car park on the ER110 / Paúl da Serra (the new shuttle system for PR6 may also apply here).
trails.parking_cost: Parking free at the upper Rabaçal car park; shuttle fee may apply if walking down from there.
trails.exposure_notes: Mostly forested levada walking with some open stretches on Paúl da Serra; the Lagoa do Vento descent has steep ground but not cliff exposure.

tunnels.notes: Headlamp recommended for the PR 6.4 (Levada Velha do Rabaçal) section.

trails.popularity_notes: The route as a single combined loop has minimal online presence (only 3 likes on the source Komoot tour) — but each component PR appears in serious hiking guides. The combined loop is a niche, slightly off-the-beaten-track alternative to the busy 25 Fontes/Risco circuit.

trails.name: Porto da Cruz to Caniçal — Vereda do Larano & Boca do Risco
trails.location: East Madeira coast (Porto da Cruz — Larano — Boca do Risco — Caniçal)
trails.status: Open (no official PR designation; no advance reservation required as of Feb 2026)
alternative_names: Vereda do Larano - Boca do Risco
Porto da Cruz – Boca do Risco – Caniçal
trails.start_point: Porto da Cruz (coastal village on the east coast)
trails.fee_amount: No fee required as of Feb 2026 — verify current status before going.
highlights: 400 m vertical cliff-edge views over the north coast
Boca do Risco mountain pass with vistas to Ponta de São Lourenço, Penha d'Águia, and (on clear days) Porto Santo island
Historic trade route once used by locals between Machico/Caniçal and Porto da Cruz
Endemic flora; mostly free of tourist crowds (often described as 'underrated')
equipment_needed: Sturdy hiking boots (not trainers) — trail gets steep and slippery
Rain jacket (weather changes fast on the north coast)
Trekking poles helpful on the descents
trails.safety_notes: Komoot rates this 'Hard' with a 'segment that may be dangerous' (alpine hiking path, ~2.37 km after the 4.63 km mark). Sure-footedness, sturdy shoes and alpine experience required. Cliff-edge sections with exposed drops of up to 400 m; not for vertigo sufferers. Trail signage is reportedly inconsistent in places — bring offline maps. Avoid in wet/windy conditions.
trails.best_season: Spring (April–May) and autumn (September–October) for stable weather and comfortable temperatures.
trails.parking_location: Limited parking near the trailhead 3 km uphill from Porto da Cruz (a small sand pit fits a few cars). Alternative: park in Porto da Cruz or Machico and use the bus.
trails.exposure_notes: Long sections run along narrow paths carved into cliffs 300–400 m above the sea; some sketchy bits have railings, others do not. The path is generally wide enough to feel safe in dry conditions but vertigo sufferers should avoid.

tunnels.notes: No major tunnels on the route itself (the old Caniçal tunnel sits near the eastern trailhead but is not walked through).

trails.popularity_notes: Has 1,221+ AllTrails reviews on the most popular variant and additional reviews across alternative versions (Porto da Cruz - Boca do Risco: 328; Larano - Pico do Furado - Pico da Coroa loop: 173). Multiple bloggers call it 'Madeira's most breathtaking coastal hike' or 'one of the most underrated hikes in Madeira'. Still noticeably less crowded than PR1/PR6/PR8.
